chart.spring: Wyckoff Spring — buyers absorbed the liquidity grab
chart.upthrust: Wyckoff Upthrust — sellers failed to hold the breakout
chart.retestBear: Bearish Retest — price broke below {{price}} and is retesting it as resistance. Former support flipped — sellers are defending this level.
chart.retestBull: Bullish Retest — price broke above {{price}} and is retesting it as support. Former resistance flipped — buyers are defending this level.
chart.obBullDesc: The last red candle before a strong up-move — institutions placed buy orders here. If price comes back, it often bounces as smart money defends their longs.
chart.obBearDesc: The last green candle before a strong down-move — institutions placed sell orders here. If price comes back, expect resistance as smart money defends their shorts.
chart.fvgBullDesc: A price gap left by a fast up-move. The market skipped over this zone — price often comes back to 'fill' it before continuing higher.
chart.fvgBearDesc: A price gap left by a fast down-move. The market skipped over this zone — price often comes back to 'fill' it before continuing lower.
chart.bslDesc: {{count}} equal highs stacked here — stop-loss orders from short sellers sit just above. Smart money often pushes price above this level to trigger those stops, then reverses down.
chart.sslDesc: {{count}} equal lows stacked here — stop-loss orders from buyers sit just below. Smart money often pushes price below this level to trigger those stops, then reverses up.
chart.eqDesc: The midpoint of the recent price range. Above this line = expensive/premium zone, where smart money prefers to sell. Below this line = cheap/discount zone, where smart money prefers to buy.
chart.oteBullDesc: ICT's 0.618–0.705 Fibonacci retracement zone. After a strong up-move, institutions wait for price to pull back into this zone to enter long at a better price.
chart.oteBearDesc: ICT's 0.618–0.705 Fibonacci retracement zone. After a strong down-move, institutions wait for price to pull back into this zone to enter short at a better price.
chart.bosBull: Break of Structure — buyers took out prior swing high
chart.bosBear: Break of Structure — sellers took out prior swing low
chart.chochBull: Change of Character — first bullish BOS, trend may be shifting
chart.chochBear: Change of Character — first bearish BOS, trend may be shifting

read.aligned: This chart and the bigger trend point the same way.
read.mixedLineDown: Short-term down, bigger picture up. Moves against the bigger trend are often short-lived, so the key question is whether this dip stalls or breaks through.
read.mixedLineLeaningDown: Short-term leaning down, bigger picture up. Moves against the bigger trend are often short-lived, so the key question is whether this dip stalls or breaks through.
read.mixedLineUp: Short-term up, bigger picture down. Moves against the bigger trend are often short-lived, so the key question is whether this bounce stalls or breaks through.
read.mixedLineLeaningUp: Short-term leaning up, bigger picture down. Moves against the bigger trend are often short-lived, so the key question is whether this bounce stalls or breaks through.
read.bigNotLoaded: The bigger-timeframe trend hasn't loaded yet.
read.bigDisagree: The bigger timeframes don't agree with each other, so this is a short-term read only.
read.trendNoSignalUp: Trend up, no clear short-term signal
read.trendNoSignalDown: Trend down, no clear short-term signal
read.shortMixed: The short-term signals point in different directions, so the bigger trend is the main guide for now.
read.nothingStands: Nothing on this chart stands out right now; the bigger trend is the main guide.
read.mixedLine: The signals point in different directions. A clean break of a key level is usually the next clue.
read.watchBounce: If the bounce clears {{res}}, it has room to run; if it fails there, the downtrend usually takes over again.
read.watchDip: If the dip holds {{sup}}, the uptrend usually resumes; a break below it would make this more than a dip.
read.watchBreakDown: A break below {{sup}} would add confirmation to the move down.
read.watchBreakUp: A break above {{res}} would add confirmation to the move up.
read.watchEither: A clean break of either level is the next clue.
read.cancelAboveChart: A move above {{price}} would cancel the chart pattern.
read.cancelBelowChart: A move below {{price}} would cancel the chart pattern.
read.cancelAboveEw: A move above {{price}} would cancel the Elliott count.
read.cancelBelowEw: A move below {{price}} would cancel the Elliott count.

mtf.allUp: All {{n}} timeframes are trending up: on each one, price is above its 20- and 50-candle averages. Buyers are in control at every level.
mtf.allDown: All {{n}} timeframes are trending down: on each one, price is below its 20- and 50-candle averages. Sellers are in control at every level.
mtf.mostUp: Most timeframes are trending up, including the 1H. The bigger picture favors buyers.
mtf.mostDown: Most timeframes are trending down, including the 1H. The bigger picture favors sellers.
mtf.upDipping: The bigger timeframes are trending up, but the 1H is dipping. In an uptrend, dips like this often get bought — many traders wait for the 1H to turn back up.
mtf.downBouncing: The bigger timeframes are trending down, but the 1H is bouncing. In a downtrend, bounces like this often fade — many traders wait for the 1H to turn back down.
mtf.leanUp: The bigger timeframes lean up; the 1H has no clear direction yet.
mtf.leanDown: The bigger timeframes lean down; the 1H has no clear direction yet.
mtf.noTrend: No clear trend across timeframes — price is mostly going sideways. The picture usually gets clearer once the bigger timeframes line up.

wiz.riskOversold: RSI {{rsi}} — oversold. Watch for a bounce before entering.
wiz.alignedBody: {{conf}} conviction {{dir}} signal. Setup favors a {{intent}} entry.
wiz.alignedBodyMtf: {{conf}} conviction {{dir}} signal with full MTF support. Setup favors a {{intent}} entry.
wiz.partialBody: Bias leans {{dir}} ({{conf}} confidence) but not all timeframes agree. Consider reduced size and wait for a cleaner trigger.
wiz.partialRisk: Mixed alignment — manage position size carefully.
wiz.rangingBody: Market is ranging. No clear signal for a {{intent}} here. Wait for a breakout or clearer structure.
wiz.waitBodyOpposing: Bias is {{bias}} ({{conf}} confidence) but HTF structure is opposing. A confirmed trigger will improve risk/reward.
wiz.waitBodyMixed: Bias is {{bias}} ({{conf}} confidence) but timeframes are mixed. A confirmed trigger will improve risk/reward.

wiz.avoidBodySell: Current signal shows {{bias}} conditions — selling or shorting here puts you against the dominant flow.
wiz.avoidHtf: HTF structure confirms the opposing direction.

daily.bullDominant: Dominant bull session — buyers controlled {{pct}}% of the range with minimal rejection. Strong momentum candle.
daily.bullUpperWick: Bulls made progress but faced late selling at the highs. Upper wick signals overhead supply — watch for retest.
daily.bullLowerWick: Intraday sell-off was fully absorbed and reversed. Demand zone confirmed at the lows — bullish structure intact.
daily.bullStrong: Strong bullish close at +{{pct}}% — buyers in full control. Continuation likely if volume holds.
daily.bullModest: Modest bullish close at +{{pct}}%. Structure favors bulls but momentum is measured — await confirmation.
daily.bearDominant: Dominant bear session — sellers controlled {{pct}}% of the range. Distribution pressure likely ongoing.
daily.bearLowerWick: Bears pushed lower but buyers defended the lows. Lower wick hints at support — potential reversal zone forming.
daily.bearUpperWick: Early buying was rejected hard. Upper wick confirms supply overhead — bearish bias carries into next session.
daily.bearHeavy: Heavy bearish close at {{pct}}% — sellers dominant. Risk-off bias until key support is reclaimed.
daily.bearMild: Mild bearish close at {{pct}}%. Bears have the edge but conviction is low — watch for early-session direction.

BearishMarubozu.name: Bearish Marubozu

Hammer.name: Hammer

HangingMan.name: Hanging Man
HangingMan.desc: Long lower wick at a high shows sellers tested lower — distribution may be starting

ShootingStar.name: Shooting Star
ShootingStar.desc: Price rallied hard then was rejected back down — market makers used the spike to dump into buyers

InvertedHammer.name: Inverted Hammer
InvertedHammer.desc: Buyers tried to push higher but gave some back — watch for follow-through confirmation

BullishEngulfing.name: Bullish Engulfing
BullishEngulfing.desc: This candle completely swallowed the previous red — buyers overwhelmed sellers, momentum has flipped

BearishEngulfing.name: Bearish Engulfing
BearishEngulfing.desc: Sellers took back everything buyers gained and more — a clean momentum shift to the downside

MorningStar.name: Morning Star
MorningStar.desc: Classic 3-candle bottom: sell pressure faded into indecision, then buyers stepped in hard — reversal confirmed

EveningStar.name: Evening Star
EveningStar.desc: 3-candle top pattern: rally stalled into a doji then sellers took over — smart money distributed into the strength

BullishPinbar.name: Bullish Pinbar

BearishPinbar.name: Bearish Pinbar

InsideTheCandle.name: Inside The Candle

SpinningTop.name: Spinning Top

ThreeWhiteSoldiers.name: Three White Soldiers

ThreeBlackCrows.name: Three Black Crows

BullishCandle.name: Bullish Candle

BearishCandle.name: Bearish Candle

ewTarget.w5eq: Last step — same size as step 1

ewStory.progressAll: Price is already at {{price}} — every target here has been reached, so this pattern has mostly played out.
ewStory.wrongAbove: If price climbs above {{price}}, this reading is wrong.
ewStory.wrongBelow: If price drops below {{price}}, this reading is wrong.
ewStory.w2: Took a breather — gave back {{pct}}% of wave 1
ewStory.w4: Another breather — gave back {{pct}}% of wave 3
ewStory.stairsUp: Think of price walking up a staircase in 5 steps: 3 big steps and 2 small rests.
ewStory.stairsDown: Think of price walking down a staircase in 5 steps: 3 big steps and 2 small rests.
ewStory.triWhat: Price is bouncing between two lines that keep getting closer — like squeezing a spring. Each swing (A to E) is smaller than the one before.
ewStory.triNextUp: A squeezed spring pops. This one is expected to pop up, about as far as the triangle was wide — toward {{price}}.
ewStory.triNextDown: A squeezed spring pops. This one is expected to pop down, about as far as the triangle was wide — toward {{price}}.
ewStory.diagWhatUp: Price went up in 5 steps, but each step had less energy — squeezed into a wedge (the two dashed lines on the chart). That's how a trend runs out of gas.
ewStory.diagWhatDown: Price went down in 5 steps, but each step had less energy — squeezed into a wedge (the two dashed lines on the chart). That's how a trend runs out of gas.
ewStory.diagNext: Wedges often snap the other way, fast — usually at least back to wave 2 ({{w2}}), passing wave 4 ({{w4}}) on the way. It can go all the way back to where the wedge started, {{start}}.
ewStory.doneWhat: {{stairs}} All 5 steps are done — like a runner after a race, the move is tired.
ewStory.doneNext: After 5 steps, price usually rests the other way in 3 moves (A, B, C), often giving back 38–62% of the whole move: about {{a}} to {{b}}. A deep rest can go all the way back to {{full}}.
ewStory.w5WhatUp: {{stairs}} Steps 1 to 4 are done. Now price is taking its last step up (wave 5).
ewStory.w5WhatDown: {{stairs}} Steps 1 to 4 are done. Now price is taking its last step down (wave 5).
ewStory.w5NextEq: Step 3 was the big one, so the last step is often about the same size as step 1 — around {{price}}.
ewStory.w5NextLong: Step 3 wasn't extra big, so the last step may be the long one — around {{price}}.
ewStory.w5Careful: Last steps can stop early, so be careful near these prices.
ewStory.w4WhatUp: {{stairs}} Steps 1, 2 and 3 are done — the big step ended at {{price}}. Now price is taking its second rest (wave 4), moving down a little.
ewStory.w4WhatDown: {{stairs}} Steps 1, 2 and 3 are done — the big step ended at {{price}}. Now price is taking its second rest (wave 4), moving up a little.
ewStory.w4NextBetweenUp: This rest usually ends between {{a}} and {{b}}. After that, one last step up (wave 5) toward {{target}} is expected.
ewStory.w4NextBetweenDown: This rest usually ends between {{a}} and {{b}}. After that, one last step down (wave 5) toward {{target}} is expected.
ewStory.w4NextAroundUp: This rest usually ends around {{a}}. After that, one last step up (wave 5) toward {{target}} is expected.
ewStory.w4NextAroundDown: This rest usually ends around {{a}}. After that, one last step down (wave 5) toward {{target}} is expected.
ewStory.w4NextSoonUp: This rest usually ends soon. After that, one last step up (wave 5) toward {{target}} is expected.
ewStory.w4NextSoonDown: This rest usually ends soon. After that, one last step down (wave 5) toward {{target}} is expected.
ewStory.flatWhatDown: After a trend, price took a sideways break in 3 moves: down (A), back up almost to where it started (B), then down again to about where A ended (C). A sideways break means the main trend is still strong.
ewStory.flatWhatUp: After a trend, price took a sideways break in 3 moves: up (A), back down almost to where it started (B), then up again to about where A ended (C). A sideways break means the main trend is still strong.
ewStory.expWhatDown: Price took a tricky break in 3 moves: down (A), then up even past where it started (B) to fool one side, then down past A (C) to fool the other. That trick often marks the end of the break.
ewStory.expWhatUp: Price took a tricky break in 3 moves: up (A), then down even past where it started (B) to fool one side, then up past A (C) to fool the other. That trick often marks the end of the break.
ewStory.zigWhatDown: After a trend, price took a quick, sharp break in 3 moves: down (A), a small bounce (B), then down again (C). That break looks finished.
ewStory.zigWhatDownPast: After a trend, price took a quick, sharp break in 3 moves: down (A), a small bounce (B), then down again past A (C). That break looks finished.
ewStory.zigWhatUp: After a trend, price took a quick, sharp break in 3 moves: up (A), a small dip (B), then up again (C). That break looks finished.
ewStory.zigWhatUpPast: After a trend, price took a quick, sharp break in 3 moves: up (A), a small dip (B), then up again past A (C). That break looks finished.
ewStory.corrNextUp: Price is now expected to turn up, often winning back 38–62% of the break: about {{a}} to {{b}}. A strong turn can go all the way back to {{full}}.
ewStory.corrNextDown: Price is now expected to turn down, often winning back 38–62% of the break: about {{a}} to {{b}}. A strong turn can go all the way back to {{full}}.

ewDesc.diagonalContractingRising: Contracting rising wedge (ending diagonal) — trend exhausted, sharp reversal toward {{price}} expected
ewDesc.diagonalContractingFalling: Contracting falling wedge (ending diagonal) — trend exhausted, sharp reversal toward {{price}} expected
ewDesc.diagonalExpandingRising: Expanding rising wedge (ending diagonal) — trend exhausted, sharp reversal toward {{price}} expected
ewDesc.diagonalExpandingFalling: Expanding falling wedge (ending diagonal) — trend exhausted, sharp reversal toward {{price}} expected
ewDesc.triangleUp: Contracting triangle (A-B-C-D-E) complete — upside breakout expected
ewDesc.triangleDown: Contracting triangle (A-B-C-D-E) complete — downside breakout expected
